blocks.text: Essential Excel shortcuts for medical receptionists on Mac
Speed matters when you have a line of patients at the front desk. Your keyboard is your fastest tool. Learn these combinations to stop reaching for your trackpad.

items: Select an entire row: Press Shift + Space.
Select an entire column: Press Control + Space.
Fill data down: Press Command + D.
Open the Format Cells dialog: Press Command + 1.
Edit the active cell: Press Fn + F2.

blocks.text: If a shortcut does not work, check your System Settings. Sometimes macOS shortcuts overlap with Excel commands. Go to System Settings > Keyboard > Shortcuts to disable conflicting keys.
Keeping patient data clean and accurate

Data entry errors are common in busy clinics. Use Data Validation to force consistent entries for items like insurance types or appointment statuses. Select the cells you want to control. Go to Data > Data Validation. Choose List from the Allow menu and type your options separated by commas.
Preventing Excel from changing your numbers

Excel often removes leading zeros from patient IDs or phone numbers. It thinks they are math values. To fix this, change the cell format to Text before you type. Select the column, go to the Home tab, click the Number Format dropdown, and choose Text. You can also type a single quote mark before the number to force it to stay as text.

Patient privacy is your priority. Always password protect your files. Go to File > Save As. Click the Options button in the save dialog. Enter a strong password under the Protection section. Save your file and store it in a secure folder.
How to handle large patient lists

When your patient list grows, use Freeze Panes to keep headers visible. Select the row below your headers. Go to View > Freeze Panes. This keeps the names and dates at the top while you scroll through hundreds of rows. Use the Filter tool by pressing Command + Shift + F to quickly find specific patient names.

faq.question: Does Excel for Mac handle large patient datasets?
faq.answer: Yes, Excel for Mac supports up to 1,048,576 rows per sheet, which is sufficient for most clinic databases.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur to edit my Excel files?
faq.answer: Lazur cannot click buttons or edit your files for you. It points at tools and guides you through the process so you can do it yourself.

faq.question: How do I make sure my patient IDs don't lose zeros?
faq.answer: Set the cell format to Text before entering your data, or start your entry with a single quote mark.
